chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated who said: Yaqoob ibn Yazid narrated from Mus'ab ibn Yazid, from Al-Awam ibn Zubayr, who said: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said:

The Riser (peace be upon him) will accept [the allegiance of] forty-five men from nine tribes: one man from one tribe, two men from a second tribe, three men from a third tribe, four men from a fourth tribe, five men from a fifth tribe, six men from a sixth tribe, seven men from a seventh tribe, eight men from an eighth tribe, and nine men from a ninth tribe, and it will remain thus until the number is completed.
ai.seo_question: How many men and from how many tribes will initially support the Qa'im?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this specific numerical structure to highlight the organized and diverse nature of the Qa'im's initial vanguard, emphasizing that the support comes from established tribal lineages rather than a random assembly. The sequential increase from one to nine men per tribe symbolizes a deliberate, expanding coalition that ensures stability and broad representation before the final gathering of the full army. This detail underscores the Shia belief in a structured, divinely ordained preparation for the global establishment of justice.
